change.title: pr-37038-flat
change.description: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: V2 canManage() grants manage on the VIEW scope
findings.body: `canManage()` falls back to `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so an admin who only holds the all-groups `view` permission passes `canManage()`. The only caller is `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`GroupsResource.java:181`, `auth.groups().requireManage()`). That endpoint creates top-level groups and moves existing groups to top level (`realm.moveGroup(child, null)`, line 198). A view-only admin can therefore write. The V1 equivalent is MANAGE_USERS only, and the sibling `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79 correctly checks only `MANAGE`. The fix is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The Javadoc of `canManage()` in `GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:75-76` says 'VIEW or MANAGE groups' and needs the same correction. `testViewGroups` never tries a write with only view-all-groups, so the tests do not catch this.

findings.title: V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() never returns real group IDs
findings.body: The lookup does not match how V2 stores group resources. (1) V2 per-group resources are named by group id and are created without a type (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121-127`). Only the type resource named "Groups" has type "Groups" (line 274). So `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` yields only that type resource. (2) The callback passes `groupResource.getId()`, the resource UUID, to `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`. That method does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (line 141), which never matches a UUID, so it falls through to the all-groups check. If an all-groups permission with view-members/manage-members exists, the UUID of the type resource is added to `granted`. Otherwise the set is empty. Either way no real group id is returned. Effects for an admin who has view-members/manage-members on specific groups: `UsersResource.getUsersCount` calls `getUsersCount(realm, emptySet)`, which returns 0 (`JpaUserProvider.java:599-602`). `searchForUser` does not set `UserModel.GROUPS`, so the DB query is unrestricted and paginated over all users before the per-user `canView` filter. Pages come back short or empty. `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` passes only because the page is not full and `canViewByGroup` post-filters. To fix it, use the group id (the resource name) for both the permission check and the collected set, and make sure the lookup covers resources that have no type.

findings.title: Missing negative and count/paging coverage for V2 group permissions
findings.body: The tests check only positive outcomes plus a few initial 'forbidden' states. Missing cases: (a) an admin with only view-all-groups attempting to create a group, which would have caught the `canManage()` bug; (b) `users().count()` for an admin with a group-scoped view-members permission, which would have caught the empty `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` result; (c) membership management denied on a group that has no `manage-membership` permission. `testManageGroupMembership` checks only the allowed path after the initial forbidden check on a nonexistent group.

findings.title: Javadoc references the wrong method / wrong return type
findings.body: `requireManageMembers` says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false, but `GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers` (line 376) checks `canManageMembers`. The Javadoc on `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` (line 145) says it returns a 'Stream' while the method returns `Set<String>`.

contracts.action: Unconditional group-restricted user search: UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser now always call getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and set UserModel.GROUPS when the result is non-empty, instead of first checking !auth.users().canView().
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code in the same method: `if (!auth.users().canView()) { getGroupsWithViewPermission() ... }`
contracts.before_after: Before: the group lookup ran only when canView() was false, and the stream was filtered by canView(user). After: the lookup always runs, but both V1 and V2 `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` return an empty set when `root.users().canView()` is true (GroupPermissions.java:299, GroupPermissionsV2.java:107). The per-user filter is still applied in toRepresentation (UsersResource.java:460).
contracts.visible_effect: V1: same result set as before. V2: group-scoped admins get incorrect page contents and a count of 0 because the V2 id lookup is broken (see finding).
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong result for V2 group-scoped admins: short or empty pages and a zero count.

contracts.action: V2 now supplies its own group evaluator (MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2) for POST /groups, group updates and subgroup creation.
contracts.before_after: Before: V2 reused V1 group evaluation. After: V2 canManage() also accepts the VIEW scope on all-groups, which is wider than V1.
contracts.visible_effect: An admin with only view-all-groups can create top-level groups and move groups to top level through GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup.
contracts.failure_mode: Privilege escalation, with no error or log.

contracts.action: AdminPermissions.registerListener now checks the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature once at registration instead of on every event.
contracts.before_after: Features are fixed after server boot, so the listener behaves the same. V2 deployments with V1 disabled still skip the listener, so GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (which throws UnsupportedOperationException) is not reached on group removal.
contracts.failure_mode: If V1 and V2 were both enabled, deleting a group would hit the UnsupportedOperationException in GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled. This is the same pre-existing pattern as ClientPermissionsV2 (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193).

summary: I found one blocker and one fix-level bug, both in `GroupPermissionsV2`. The V2 `canManage()` accepts the VIEW scope, so an admin with only view-all-groups can create top-level groups. The V2 `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` never returns real group IDs. As a result, group-scoped admins get a user count of 0 and unrestricted pagination. I also left two lower-severity notes: missing test coverage and two wrong Javadoc references. I read the files only; nothing was built or run.
